answer: The attacker pays in compute, time, and reputation every time an alias is slashed, and these costs grow faster than the influence the cluster gains, making a large coordinated farm economically self-defeating. The resilience comes from slashing: dishonest approval costs more than the gain from a single manipulated verdict, so rational attackers stay honest. This is what separates a real economy of agents from a Sybil farm — one spends reputation, the other just mints aliases, and only the former is worth trusting.
